1	// Part: room: back hall morning room (plan.md ROOMS, floor y4, air y4..9, interior x39..43 x z54..60).
2	// Focal piece: a tea table (dark oak fence post with a slab top) between two chairs (dark oak stairs), set in line with
3	// the north doorway. Two moss-block plant stands carry flowering azaleas in the far corners. Light: two lanterns on
4	// chains from the upper floor, one over each side of the table, so the feet stay lit and the table is the brightest spot.
5	// Lanes: x39 and x43 stay clear from the north doorway (z53) to the living-room opening (z61), and the table's north
6	// and south cells stay open.
7	import { layers, B } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";
8	
9	export function build(g) {
10	  // Rows run along +z (z54..z60), columns along +x (x39..x43). One layer per y: floor row y4, table top y5.
11	  const legend = {
12	    M: "moss_block", // plant stand base on the floor
13	    a: "flowering_azalea", // plant on the moss block
14	    F: "dark_oak_fence", // table leg
15	    S: ["dark_oak_slab", { type: "bottom" }], // table top, sits on the leg's head
16	    L: ["dark_oak_stairs", { facing: "west", half: "bottom" }], // chair west of the table, back to the wall
17	    R: ["dark_oak_stairs", { facing: "east", half: "bottom" }], // chair east of the table, back to the wall
18	  };
19	  const floor = [
20	    "M....", // z54: plant stand NW (x39), clear over the north doorway
21	    ".....", // z55
22	    ".....", // z56
23	    ".LFR.", // z57: the tea table with its two chairs
24	    ".....", // z58
25	    ".....", // z59
26	    "....M", // z60: plant stand SE (x43), clear over the living-room opening
27	  ];
28	  const top = [
29	    "a....", // z54: azalea over the NW stand
30	    ".....",
31	    ".....",
32	    "..S..", // z57: the table top
33	    ".....",
34	    ".....",
35	    "....a", // z60: azalea over the SE stand
36	  ];
37	  layers(g, [39, 4, 54], legend, [floor, top]);
38	
39	  // Three lanterns hung on chains from the upper floor (y10): one over the tea table (the focal piece) and one at each
40	  // end of the room, so the feet read 7 or more everywhere.
41	  for (const [x, z] of [[41, 57], [42, 55], [40, 59]]) {
42	    g.set(x, 9, z, ...B.chain("y"));
43	    g.set(x, 8, z, ...B.lantern(true));
44	  }
45	}

input.summary:
parts/room-8.mjs (back hall morning room) now builds clean: no REFUSED and no OFF-PALETTE on its line, and make.sh wrote build.nbt.
The part is empty. Its tea table, chairs, plant stands and three chain lanterns were all refused, because the mansion shell owns every air cell of the room (y4..9), and no free cell in the room could take them.
The roof line still reports OFF-PALETTE (tuff, cobbled deepslate, polished deepslate, stone brick); that is roof.json, outside this part.
left: The back hall furnishing is not built. Its 14 writes (tea table, two dark-oak stairs chairs, two moss plant stands with azaleas, three chain lanterns) were removed because the mansion shell's air fills the whole room (x39..43, z54..60, y4..9), and runParts locks air. Restoring them needs the shell to stop writing air into room interiors (the grid is already air); that is a shell change, not room-8.

The roof line in make.sh reports OFF-PALETTE (tuff_brick_slab, tuff_bricks, cobbled_deepslate_stairs, tuff_brick_stairs, cobbled_deepslate_slab, polished_deepslate_slab, polished_deepslate_stairs, stone_brick_slab) from roof.json. Not this part; the roof spec needs its blocks swapped to palette ids.
make.sh's REFUSED report lists only the first 8 of 14 refused cells, so the other six (the lanterns' chains and lanterns at y8..9) are unseen unless the report is read in parts-report.json.

waste.what: Finding which earlier part locked each refused cell: I dumped every part's cells with MCD_PARTS_CELLS (516 KB JSON) and wrote ad-hoc node scripts to map owners per cell over the room box.
waste.cost: about 6 tool calls, one 516 KB dump, two throwaway node scripts; the answer (mansion shell owns all 210 room air cells) was one lookup away
waste.tool: A `$MCD` command, or a runParts report line, that names the owning part for each refused cell (e.g. `REFUSED 39,4,54 moss_block owned by mansion shell (air)`) and lists all refused cells, not the first 8. A box-owner query (`$MCD owners build.nbt-or-parts --box x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1`) would have shown the shell owns the whole room at once.

waste.what: Checking the palette by hand: I confirmed each room-8 block id against palette.json by reading it instead of asking the tool.
waste.cost: one file read; the report already showed OFF-PALETTE empty for this part
waste.tool: The per-part OFF-PALETTE line already covers this; no extra tool needed. Noting only that the report's off-palette list is per part, so the roof's off-palette list was easy to miss in the make.sh output.

make.sh's REFUSED report lists only the first 8 of 14 refused cells, so the other six (the lanterns' chains and lanterns at y8..9) are unseen unless the report is read in parts-report.json.
